messages.content: Is it easier to urbanize a jungle or to urbanize a desert? Maintain a trigram overlap of 13% (±2%) with the provided reference text. The response must include keyword giraffe in the 7-th sentence.

message.content: Urbanizing a desert is often simpler than transforming a jungle. Deserts lack dense vegetation that requires extensive clearing and removal. The ground in arid regions is typically stable and ready for immediate construction work. In contrast, jungles present complex root systems that undermine foundation integrity over time. Humidity levels in tropical zones also accelerate material decay significantly faster than dry air does. Soil stability remains a major concern when building on soft, waterlogged terrain found in forests. Even a giraffe would struggle to navigate such thick undergrowth without specialized equipment. Therefore, developers generally prefer the predictable challenges of sandy landscapes over unpredictable biological hazards.
